clue.text: Revolver carried in one's boot as a precaution?

definitions.text: Revolver carried in one's boot as a precaution?

parts.words: Revolver carried in one's boot as a precaution?
parts.note: the revolver is not a gun but something that turns round, and the boot is a car's luggage space, where a motorist keeps a standby tyre

explanation.surface: A cautious gunslinger hides a pistol in a cowboy boot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolver' and 'boot' both suggest a gunfighter; in Britain the boot is the luggage compartment of a car.
explanation.definitionFit: A standby tyre kept in the car for punctures turns as it rolls, so it is a revolver carried in case of need.

clue.text: Show displeasure when nothing is in place

indicators.note: the word for nothing sits inside the word for place

parts.note: to place something is to put it
O, the figure zero, means nothing

explanation.surface: Someone sulks whenever nothing is where it should be.
explanation.definitionFit: To push out the lips sulkily is a way of showing displeasure.

clue.text: Very much like sauce

explanation.surface: A sauce that someone is very fond of.
explanation.definitionFit: To enjoy something greatly is to savour it, and a tangy pickle or chutney served with food is also called by this word.

clue.text: Don grew upset and aggrieved

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are knocked over and rearranged, as an upset tray is

explanation.surface: A university don becomes annoyed and feels hard done by.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' looks like part of the don's mood, but it rearranges DONGREW.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone treated unjustly feels hard done by, which is what aggrieved means here.

clue.text: Point of issue

parts.note: read not as the matter under debate but as the place where people issue, that is go out

explanation.surface: The key matter in an argument.
explanation.definitionFit: A doorway out of a building is the spot where people issue forth.

clue.text: Lear production upset part of Hamlet

indicators.note: a new staging of the play reshuffles its title letters

parts.note: split as up plus set: in a down clue, set written upwards

explanation.surface: A staging of King Lear disrupts a role in Hamlet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'production' rearranges LEAR into LAER; 'upset' is read as 'set' going up the grid, giving TES.
explanation.definitionFit: Laertes is a role in Shakespeare's tragedy, Ophelia's brother who duels with the prince.

clue.text: Warmer, in the main

parts.note: the main is the old poetic word for the open sea, and the warmer is a current that heats it

explanation.surface: It is generally rather warmer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the main' poses as 'generally', but the main is the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: The Atlantic current flowing from the Caribbean towards Europe warms the seas and western coasts it reaches.

clue.text: Indifference to detail

explanation.surface: Someone shows no interest in the fine points.
explanation.definitionFit: Aloofness is lack of emotional involvement, and a military detail is a small unit sent off on a task, both called by this word.

clue.text: Clever stroke to point

parts.note: a cut is a stroke of a blade or bat
E, east, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A smart shot with a sharp end.
explanation.definitionFit: Sharp-witted and shrewd, as in a cute move.

clue.text: Parliamentary device that heads off further debate?

definitions.text: Parliamentary device that heads off further debate?

parts.words: Parliamentary device that heads off further debate?
parts.note: a procedural motion to cut short discussion of a bill, with heads off read literally as removing heads

explanation.surface: A procedural rule that prevents more argument in the Commons.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain's Parliament a timetable motion that ends debate on stages of a bill is named after the French beheading machine.
explanation.definitionFit: The parliamentary time limit shares its name with the blade apparatus of the French Revolution, which literally took heads off.

clue.text: A binding affair is arranged

indicators.note: the letters of the word are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A marriage of convenience has been set up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'binding affair' looks like a wedding; 'is arranged' rearranges AFFAIR.
explanation.definitionFit: Palm-leaf fibre is used for tying plants and parcels, so it is a binding material.

clue.text: Sack for someone who takes money

explanation.surface: Firing the person at the till.
explanation.definitionFit: To dismiss an officer from the armed forces is one sense; a bank or shop clerk handling payments is the other.

clue.text: Swindles, theft and intrigue

parts.note: cons are swindles or tricks
piracy is theft, at sea or of copyright

explanation.surface: Fraud, stealing and plotting go together.
explanation.definitionFit: A secret plot by several people is a scheme or intrigue.

clue.text: Appears to accept poetry of acceptable quality

indicators.note: one word takes in, or accepts, the other inside it

parts.note: seems means appears
lines are verses of poetry

explanation.surface: Someone seems willing to accept verse of decent standard.
explanation.definitionFit: Propriety, the quality of being fitting and decorous, makes behaviour acceptable.

clue.text: Course must be if you steer wrongly

definitions.text: Course must be if you steer wrongly

indicators.note: the letters of the word are put wrongly, so rearranged

explanation.surface: A navigator who goes astray has to put the ship's heading right again.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition and the wordplay: rearranging STEER gives the word for setting a course afresh.
explanation.definitionFit: Steering off line means the heading has to be set again, adjusted afresh.

clue.text: Two points in a dog delight

indicators.note: the pair of letters goes inside the word for the dog

parts.note: a bitch is a female dog
E and W, east and west, are two compass points

explanation.surface: A dog with two sharp points brings joy.
explanation.definitionFit: To enchant or charm someone, as if casting a spell, is to delight them.

clue.text: Central heating system in the red

definitions.text: Central heating system in the red

parts.words: Central heating system in the red
parts.note: not a boiler and radiators run at a loss, but the red fluid that carries body warmth around

explanation.surface: A home heating installation that is costing too much.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the red' suggests debt; it describes the fluid's colour.
explanation.definitionFit: The red fluid circulating from the heart distributes warmth through the body, a central heating system.

clue.text: Gives the players a hand

parts.note: not helping or applauding a team, but handing out cards to everyone at the table

explanation.surface: Someone helps out or applauds the performers.
explanation.definitionFit: At cards, the dealer distributes each player's hand.

clue.text: You want to be in it

definitions.text: You want to be in it

parts.words: You want to be in it
parts.note: not a desire to join something, but being in a state of lacking, where you want in the sense of lack

explanation.surface: Something everyone wishes to belong to.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in want or poverty is to be in this state, and want means lack.

clue.text: He's on about being present

parts.note: he taken as written, with the 's as a link
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A man keeps going on about being there.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in attendance, at this place, is to be present.

clue.text: The doctor joins me in a drink

parts.note: doc is short for doctor

explanation.surface: The GP and I share a glass of something.
explanation.definitionFit: A red Bordeaux wine from the left bank of the Gironde is a drink.

clue.text: Meal set out for cross islanders

indicators.note: the letters are put out of their order and rearranged

explanation.surface: A dinner is put out for some angry people from an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cross' looks like 'angry', but it is the eight-pointed cross of the Knights of Malta; the island was also awarded the George Cross.
explanation.definitionFit: People of Malta, the Mediterranean island whose emblem is an eight-pointed cross, are so named.

clue.text: Hold on, I can't move!

indicators.note: the letters move about into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone cries out to wait because they are stuck fast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hold on' reads as 'wait', but 'Hold' alone is the definition and ON joins the anagram of I CANT.
explanation.definitionFit: To hold something is to have it inside, to enclose it.

clue.text: But Arctic fur doesn't come from it

definitions.text: But Arctic fur doesn't come from it

parts.words: But Arctic fur doesn't come from it
parts.note: a cat linked to the Pole might be expected to give Arctic fur, but this animal is a weasel of temperate woods

explanation.surface: A remark about where polar pelts are not sourced.
explanation.walkthrough: The animal's name suggests a cat from the North Pole; it is a European weasel relative, famous for its smell.
explanation.definitionFit: A dark-furred mustelid of European woodland, related to the ferret, despite its name has no Arctic connection.

clue.text: Step on it before the opening

definitions.text: Step on it before the opening

parts.words: Step on it before the opening
parts.note: step on it means hurry, but here the instruction is literal: tread on this mat placed by the doorway

explanation.surface: Hurry up before the show starts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Step on it' poses as 'go faster'; the opening is a door.
explanation.definitionFit: A mat for wiping shoes lies at the threshold, trodden on before passing through.

clue.text: About to sit and take it easy

parts.note: re means about or concerning
to sit for a portrait is to pose

explanation.surface: A model is about to sit down and relax.
explanation.definitionFit: To rest or lie quietly is to relax, take it easy.

clue.text: Note sent back for the cheesemaker

indicators.note: the word for the banknote is sent back, read from the end

parts.note: a tenner is a ten-pound banknote

explanation.surface: Money is returned to the dairy farmer.
explanation.walkthrough: A tenner is British slang for a ten-pound note.
explanation.definitionFit: The curdling agent from calves' stomachs is what turns milk into curds, the cheesemaker's essential.

clue.text: Boss seen in a boiled shirt

explanation.surface: The man in charge wears a starched evening shirt.
explanation.walkthrough: A boiled shirt is a stiff, starched formal shirt, fastened with small decorative buttons.
explanation.definitionFit: A boss is a raised knob or ornament, and the detachable button fastening a starched dress shirt is also this word.

clue.text: Measure encountered over the East

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits over, above, the second

parts.note: met means encountered
E is short for east

explanation.surface: A measurement taken on meeting someone over in the Orient.
explanation.definitionFit: To dole out or allot, usually punishment, is to measure out.

clue.text: Additional protection for a cricketer

explanation.surface: A cricketer is given more padding.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a fielding position on the off side between cover and mid-off is named this way, and so is the player there.
explanation.definitionFit: More insurance or shielding is one sense; a fielder stationed in that off-side position is the other.

clue.text: Actors in form

explanation.surface: Performers are on good form.
explanation.definitionFit: The company of performers in a play is one sense; a mould or shape is the other.

clue.text: Put in a difficult position when a tip gave offence

parts.note: an end is a tip, as of a finger
angered means offended, gave offence to

explanation.surface: A waiter's small gratuity upset a customer, making things awkward.
explanation.definitionFit: To put at risk or in peril is to place in a difficult position.
